newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks continue retreat at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks continue retreat at open.

text.p: The Australian sharemarket dived at the open on Tuesday, driven down by a weaker Wall Street with Commonwealth Bank going ex-dividend accelerating the fall.
At open, the All Ordinaries index was down 16.6 points at 2,265.5. The September share index futures were 17 points down at 2,270, a 4.5 point premium to the index.
With long-dated U.S. bond yields touching seven percent and the local bond market sliding in sympathy, brokers said there remained little in the way of positive signs to inspire investors.
"Except for gold everything is pointing down today," said a Sydney broker.
"The Dow and bonds are both off and a major stock like Commonwealth Bank going ex-dividend is just helping it down."
Underlying the paucity of positive signs, the gold index bucked the trend to edge just higher.
Aluminium producer Comalco Ltd continued to lose ground, dropping over three percent after Monday's sharply lower first half net profit of A$50.6 million on a joint venture basis.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about two to one, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
